metadata.summary: Paris Fury has retracted her claim that husband Tyson Fury was diagnosed with schizophrenia.
metadata.content: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Paris Fury retracts claim her husband has been diagnosed with schizophrenia | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Paris Fury retracts claim her husband has been diagnosed with schizophrenia Paris Fury says Tyson did not receive a diagnosis of schizophrenia; Netflix documentary has now been updated; The British Boxing Board of Control indicated it would look into comments about a schizophrenia diagnosis and could deny Fury a licence to face Anthony Joshua on December 11 Thursday 26 November 2026 23:20, UK Image: Tyson Fury has previously spoken about his struggles with mental health Paris Fury has retracted her claim that husband Tyson Fury was diagnosed with schizophrenia. A new Netflix documentary explores Tyson Fury's experiences of depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder, which became particularly acute after his unified heavyweight championship victory over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015. Paris Fury made the comments about schizophrenia in an initial version of the documentary. Netflix said it has worked to "update" the footage in light of her clarification. She has now said: "I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary. I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson's condition and I used the word 'schizophrenic'.
